title: The system
subtitle: What lighthouse is made of, what works today, and what comes next.

parts.label: Binary
parts.what: One program, lighthouse, that you install once. It carries the commands below and the packs.
parts.when: Every time you run a lighthouse command.
parts.without: Each repo would need its own copies of the scripts, and they would drift apart.

parts.label: Installer (init)
parts.what: Copies the skills, hooks and working agreements from the packs into your repo, and keeps them up to date.
parts.when: Once when you start, and again with init --upgrade after a new version.
parts.without: You would copy files by hand and miss updates.

parts.label: Usage meter (usage)
parts.what: Measures how much of your Claude and Codex usage window is left, and raises an alarm when it runs low.
parts.when: Before and during agent work, read by the usage guard.
parts.without: An agent would run out of usage halfway through a task.

parts.label: Dashboard (serve)
parts.what: A small web server with a page that shows open questions, returned issues and the usage window.
parts.when: While agents work, so you see what waits for you.
parts.without: You would look through GitHub yourself to find what needs an answer.

parts.label: Controller (tick)
parts.what: Will pick up issues from the board and start agent sessions on its own. Today tick only checks the repos in [dispatch] and reads their board: it does not pick up issues or start sessions yet.
parts.when: On a timer, every few minutes.

parts.label: Packs
parts.what: The skills, hooks and rules lighthouse carries, in a core pack and a pack per language.
parts.when: Whenever init installs or upgrades a repo.
parts.without: The installer would have nothing to install.

parts.label: Your repo
parts.what: Your own project, after init has put the skills chain and the guardrails in it.
parts.when: Every time you or an agent works on the project.
parts.without: Lighthouse would have nowhere to work.

parts.label: Skills chain
parts.what: The steps an agent follows from issue to merged pull request: start, plan, build, verify, close.
parts.when: From the moment an agent picks up an issue until it is closed.
parts.without: Each agent would work its own way, and steps like review and tests would get skipped.

parts.label: Guardrails
parts.what: Hooks that stop an agent from doing harm, such as a commit on main, and run the tests after a commit.
parts.when: On every commit, push, edit and session end of an agent.
parts.without: A mistake would land on main without anyone noticing.

parts.label: Environment today
parts.what: One Linux machine that runs lighthouse serve as a systemd service, reachable over Tailscale.
parts.when: All the time, as the home of the dashboard.
parts.without: The dashboard would only run while you start it by hand.

parts.label: Second environment
parts.what: Lighthouse on a second machine or for a second user, installed without a clone.
parts.when: Once someone besides the owner uses lighthouse.
parts.without: Lighthouse only works on the machine it was built on.

parts.label: Research Cloud workspace
parts.what: Lighthouse in a SURF Research Cloud workspace, so researchers can use it there.
parts.when: When you work in SURF Research Cloud.
parts.without: Researchers on SURF Research Cloud would set everything up by hand.

parts.label: Docs and site
parts.what: The install and getting-started guides, the reference pages and this site with its maps.
parts.when: When you install lighthouse, learn how it works, or look up a rule.
parts.without: Only the owner would know how lighthouse works.
